business_model.claim: DiamondRock Hospitality Company operates as a self-managed lodging REIT that owns hotels and resorts, leases them to taxable REIT subsidiaries, and engages independent third-party managers rather than operating properties itself.
quotes: DiamondRock Hospitality Company is a self-managed and self-administered lodging-focused REIT that owns a portfolio of premium hotels and resorts.
All of our hotels are managed by a third party, either an independent operator or a brand operator, such as Marriott.
As of December 31, 2025, we leased all of our hotels to TRS lessees, except for one hotel that is directly owned by a TRS.

business_model.claim: The company owns 35 premium hotels with 9,479 rooms concentrated in U.S. leisure destinations and top gateway markets, including a 79-room resort acquired for $31.0 million.
quotes: DiamondRock Hospitality Company is a self-advised real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns a leading portfolio of geographically diversified hotels concentrated in leisure destinations and top gateway markets.
The Company owns 35 premium quality hotels with 9,479 rooms.
On October 1, 2026, the Company acquired The Bellmoor Inn & Spa, a 79-room independent resort in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, for total consideration of $31.0 million.

business_model.basis: Stated in [P1], [P4], and the property schedule in [P6].
business_model.claim: Nearly 40% of the portfolio operates as independent hotels, while the remainder operates under global lodging brands including Marriott, Hilton, IHG, and Margaritaville.
quotes: Each hotel is positioned to maximize its cash flow and value; accordingly, we choose to operate nearly 40% of our portfolio as independent hotels, with the remainder operating under a brand owned by one of the leading global lodging brand companies.

We leverage the leading global hotel brands at many of our hotels, which are flagged under a brand owned by Marriott International, Inc. (“Marriott”), Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. (“Hilton”) or IHG Hotels & Resorts (“IHG”).

business_model.claim: The company generates revenue from hotel operations—primarily room stays, which accounted for approximately 65% of total revenues, alongside food and beverage and other guest services such as parking, spa, resort fees, and tenant leases.
quotes: Our revenue is primarily derived from hotel operations, including but not limited to, rooms revenue, food and beverage revenue and other operating revenue, which consists of parking, spa, resort fees, other guest services, and tenant leases.

Room revenue comprised approximately 65% of our total revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and is dictated by demand, as measured by occupancy percentage, pricing, as measured by ADR, and our available supply of hotel rooms.

business_model.claim: Total revenues of $874,053 (table in thousands) consisted of $567,205 from rooms, 220,115 from food and beverage, and 86,733 from other revenues (table in thousands).
The hotels sell rooms and event services to individual leisure and business transient travelers as well as group and conference customers, with most properties marketed to higher-income consumers.
quotes: Our hotels face competition for individual guests, group reservations and conference business.
Our portfolio is relatively insulated from competitive new supply and the majority of our hotels are marketed to higher-income consumers.
We delivered another strong quarter, exceeding our expectations with healthy demand and higher rates across both transient and group segments.

business_model.claim: Rooms are distributed through global hotel brands' reservation and loyalty systems as well as third-party internet travel intermediaries such as Expedia.com and Priceline.com.
quotes: We believe these global brands' reservation systems and national advertising, marketing and promotional services combined with strong management by third-party operators enable our properties to perform favorably in terms of both occupancy and room rates relative to other brands and non-branded hotels.

Many of our managers and franchisors contract with third-party internet travel intermediaries, including, but not limited to, Expedia.com and Priceline.com, to sell rooms to leisure travelers, as well as for corporate and group travel.

business_model.claim: Hotel revenues move primarily with occupancy, Average Daily Rate (ADR), and available room supply, which are sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, seasonality, new hotel supply, alternative lodging, and reduced business travel from video conferencing.
quotes: Our ADR, occupancy percentage, RevPAR, and Total RevPAR performance may be impacted by macroeconomic factors such as U.S. economic conditions generally, inflation, interest rates, tariffs, regional and local employment growth, personal income and corporate earnings, office vacancy rates and business relocation decisions, airport and other business and leisure travel, increased use of lodging alternatives, new hotel construction and the pricing strategies of our competitors.

The increased use of video conferencing technology by businesses has resulted in decreased business travel as companies have leveraged the use of technologies that allow multiple parties from different locations to participate in virtual meetings without traveling to a centralized meeting location, such as our hotels.

business_model.claim: Non-room revenues and property cash flows are also driven by banquets, catering, spa, parking, and resort fees, alongside active asset management initiatives such as renovations, rebrandings, and space repurposing.
quotes: The increase was attributable to growth in banquets, catering, and service charge revenues, offset by a decrease of $5.7 million due to our 2025 Disposition.

Other revenues, which primarily represent spa, parking, resort fees and attrition and cancellation fees, increased $4.5 million from the year ended December 31, 2024 to the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to an increase in spa revenue, parking revenue, and resort fees, including the implementation of a resort fee at the Bourbon Orleans Hotel and The Lindy Renaissance Charleston Hotel.

Our asset management team also focuses on identifying new and potential value creation opportunities across our portfolio, including implementing resort or amenity fees where appropriate, creating incremental guest rooms, leasing out restaurants to more profitable third-party operators, converting underutilized space to revenue-generating meeting space, marketing underutilized midweek bookings and implementing programs to reduce energy consumption and increase labor efficiency.

business_model.claim: Property-level operating costs consist of rooms and food and beverage departmental expenses, support expenses (such as sales and marketing, administration, IT, repairs and maintenance, and utilities), and fixed property costs (such as property taxes, insurance, and ground leases).
quotes: Our operating costs and expenses consist of the costs to provide hotel services, including rooms expense, food and beverage expense, other departmental and support expenses, management and franchise fees, and other property-level expenses.

Other departmental and support expenses include labor and other costs associated with the other operating department revenue, as well as labor and other costs associated with administrative departments, sales and marketing, information technology systems, repairs and maintenance and utility costs.
Other property-level expenses include property taxes, insurance, ground lease expense, and other fixed costs.

business_model.claim: The company pays third-party management companies base and incentive fees tied to individual hotel revenues and profitability, and pays franchisors royalty, marketing, and reservation fees based on a percentage of room revenue and, at certain hotels, food and beverage revenue.
quotes: The management companies typically earn base and incentive management fees based on the levels of revenues and profitability of each individual hotel.
Franchise fees are based on a percentage of room revenue, and for certain hotels, additional franchise fees are charged for food and beverage revenue.

business_model.claim: Operating margins and profitability are driven by cost pressures in labor, utilities, and property taxes, amplified by the high fixed costs of premium full-service hotels during downturns.
quotes: Travel demand is expected to remain relatively steady in 2026 with RevPAR growth driven primarily by higher rates; however, elevated operating costs, particularly related to labor, utilities, and property taxes are expected to continue to pressure hotel profitability and operating margins.
In periods of weak demand, profitability is negatively affected by the relatively high fixed costs of operating premium full-service hotels as compared to other classes of hotels.

competitive_position.claim: Hotels face localized competition from existing and new full-service, select-service, and extended-stay properties, where material increases in new room supply can quickly depress RevPAR and profitability.
quotes: Competition is specific to the individual markets in which our properties are located and will include competition from existing and new hotels operated under brands in the full-service, select-service and extended-stay segments.
A material increase in the supply of new hotel rooms to a market can quickly destabilize that market and existing hotels can experience rapidly decreasing RevPAR and profitability.

competitive_position.claim: Alternative lodging providers such as Airbnb, alternative event platforms such as Convene, online travel intermediaries, and AI-driven booking or recommendation tools from major technology companies threaten occupancy, room rates, brand value, and profitability.
quotes: In addition to competing with traditional hotels and lodging facilities, we compete with alternative lodging, including third-party providers of short-term rental properties and serviced apartments, such as Airbnb, as well as alternative meeting and event space platforms, such as Convene.

An increase in hotel reservations made through these companies, including those that deploy artificial intelligence or automated recommendation tools, such as Google, Apple, Amazon or Meta, may reduce the value of our franchise brands, which may negatively affect our average rates and revenues.
If bookings shift to higher cost distribution channels, including these internet travel intermediaries, it could materially impact our profitability.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 risk factors)
competitive_position.claim: REIT rules bar DiamondRock from operating hotels directly, leaving daily pricing and operations to third-party managers while exposing franchised properties to brand termination risks.
quotes: In order to qualify as a REIT, we cannot operate our hotel properties or control the daily operations of our hotel properties and therefore our TRS lessees must enter into third-party hotel management agreements with one or more eligible independent contractors.

Thus, even if we believe that our hotel properties are being operated inefficiently or in a manner that does not result in satisfactory occupancy rates, ADRs and operating profits, we may not have sufficient rights under our hotel management agreements to enable us to force the hotel management company to change its method of operation.

If we were to lose a franchise or hotel brand for a particular hotel, it could harm the operation, financing, or value of that hotel due to the loss of the franchise or hotel brand name, marketing support and centralized reservation system, all or any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and our ability to make distributions to stockholders.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 risk factors and P3 2026 outlook)
competitive_position.claim: Concentration in premium full-service hotels creates high fixed-cost exposure during downturns, while elevated labor, utility, and property tax costs, tariffs, and weaker international travel threaten demand and operating margins.
quotes: In periods of weak demand, profitability is negatively affected by the relatively high fixed costs of operating premium full-service hotels as compared to other classes of hotels.

Travel demand is expected to remain relatively steady in 2026 with RevPAR growth driven primarily by higher rates; however, elevated operating costs, particularly related to labor, utilities, and property taxes are expected to continue to pressure hotel profitability and operating margins.

Given that our hotels are concentrated in major urban markets and destination resort locations in the U.S., our business may be particularly sensitive to changes in foreign exchange rates, elevated interest rates or a negative international perception of the U.S. arising from its political or other positions.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 risk factors)
competitive_position.claim: Ongoing renovation capital needs compete with REIT rules requiring distribution of at least 90% of REIT taxable income, while ground-lease transfer consents and long-term management or franchise agreements can limit hotel sales.
quotes: In addition, we may not be able to fund capital improvements or acquisitions solely from cash provided from our operating activities because we generally must distribute at least 90% of our REIT taxable income each year to maintain our REIT tax status.
These provisions of our ground leases may limit our ability to sell our hotels which, in turn, could adversely impact the price realized from any such sale.

Only two of our hotels have long-term management agreements with remaining terms in excess of five years, with the longest remaining term of 33 years, and certain of our properties have franchise agreements with terms up to 25 years, and these term lengths may deter some potential purchasers and could adversely impact the price realized from any such sale, or our ability to sell such hotels at all.

Our asset management team also focuses on identifying new and potential value creation opportunities across our portfolio, including implementing resort or amenity fees where appropriate, creating incremental guest rooms, leasing out restaurants to more profitable third-party operators, converting underutilized space to revenue-generating meeting space, marketing underutilized midweek bookings and implementing programs to reduce energy consumption and increase labor efficiency.

Thus, third-party hotel management companies that enter into management contracts with our TRS lessees control the daily operations of our hotel properties.

growth_thesis.claim: Portfolio reinvestment, renovations, and rebrandings drive future earnings growth, with $59.2 million invested in capital improvements during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and $75.0 to $80.0 million expected for full-year 2026.
quotes: The Company invested $59.2 million in capital improvements during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
The Company currently expects to invest approximately $75.0 to $80.0 million in capital improvements at its hotels in 2026.

We expect to grow earnings through continued operating execution and the ramp of our recently renovated hotels, while our free cash flow and balance sheet provide significant flexibility to deploy capital at attractive returns.
We completed rebrandings at seven of our hotels since 2021.

Our goal is to drive long-term stockholder returns that exceed those generated by our peers by growing free cash flow through disciplined capital allocation, including reinvestment in our portfolio and capital recycling, while returning capital through share repurchases and dividends.

quotes: In order to qualify as a REIT, we cannot operate our hotel properties or control the daily operations of our hotel properties and therefore our TRS lessees must enter into third-party hotel management agreements with one or more eligible independent contractors.
As of the date of this report, 18 of our 35 hotels operate under Marriott, Hilton, or IHG franchise agreements.

If we were to lose a franchise or hotel brand for a particular hotel, it could harm the operation, financing, or value of that hotel due to the loss of the franchise or hotel brand name, marketing support and centralized reservation system, all or any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and our ability to make distributions to stockholders.

risks.claim: New hotel construction, online travel intermediaries, peer-to-peer lodging platforms, and video conferencing technology threaten DiamondRock's occupancy, room rates, and distribution costs.
quotes: A material increase in the supply of new hotel rooms to a market can quickly destabilize that market and existing hotels can experience rapidly decreasing RevPAR and profitability.

Increasing use of these alternative facilities and Internet travel intermediaries could materially and adversely affect the occupancy at our hotels and could put downward pressure on average rates and revenues.

To the extent that such technologies, or new technologies, continue to play a role in day-to-day business interactions and the necessity for business-related travel decreases, demand for hotel rooms may decrease, which may have a material adverse effect on our hotels, our results of operations and our financial condition.

risks.claim: Hotels located in coastal, seismic, and major metropolitan markets—which generated 71% of total revenues in 2025—face natural disaster, climate, pandemic, and terrorism risks that may exceed insurance coverage.
quotes: Our hotels are exposed to risks from natural disasters, including earthquakes, storms, hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and rising sea levels particularly as a result of climate change.
In addition, several of our hotels are in major metropolitan markets that have been, or may be, targets of terrorist attacks or active shooter incidents.
These hotels constitute 71% of our total revenues in 2025.
In the event of an uninsured or underinsured loss, we could lose invested capital and future revenue from affected properties, and may remain liable for any related debt.

risks.claim: Cybersecurity breaches affecting DiamondRock, its third-party hotel managers, or technology vendors could disrupt hotel operations, compromise guest data, and trigger uninsured legal or remediation costs.
quotes: The risk of a cybersecurity incident continues to increase as the number, intensity and sophistication of attempted attacks and intrusions from around the world has increased.

Despite various precautionary steps to protect our hotels from losses resulting from cybersecurity incidents, any occurrence of a cybersecurity incident could still result in losses at our properties, which could affect our results of operations.
However, these insurance policies may not be adequate to cover all losses relating to cybersecurity incidents.

risks.claim: Real estate illiquidity, REIT tax holding restrictions, long-term management or franchise contracts, and lessor consent requirements on ground leases can delay or reduce proceeds from hotel sales.
quotes: In particular, the tax laws applicable to REITs require that we hold our hotels for investment, rather than primarily for sale in the ordinary course of business, which may cause us to forego or defer sales of hotels that would otherwise be in our best interests.
These provisions of our ground leases may limit our ability to sell our hotels which, in turn, could adversely impact the price realized from any such sale.

Only two of our hotels have long-term management agreements with remaining terms in excess of five years, with the longest remaining term of 33 years, and certain of our properties have franchise agreements with terms up to 25 years, and these term lengths may deter some potential purchasers and could adversely impact the price realized from any such sale, or our ability to sell such hotels at all.
